title: The Rains Fail Again
text: For the third season the sky over {province} has stayed hard and white. The barley stands thin in the fields, and the old women say the gods have turned their faces away from {realm}.

title: No Tin From the East
text: The caravans that carried tin from beyond the rivers have stopped coming. Without tin there is no bronze, and without bronze there are no spears. The smiths of {realm} sit idle.

options.label: Send to the hill smiths for iron

title: The Black Metal
text: A soot-stained smith from the hill country stands before {ruler}. He works a dark metal that needs no tin, only charcoal, bellows and patience. 'Give me a forge,' he says, 'and I will arm your sons.'

options.label: Bronze is the metal of the gods

title: Black Ships Off the Coast
text: Fishermen from {province} report long ships with bird-headed prows beating along the shore. They carry warriors in horned helmets, women and children, and everything they own.

options.label: Let them come. We will be waiting.

title: Ash in the Megaron
text: In the burned palace of {province}, scribes dig through the ash and find the old tablets: lists of rations, of chariot wheels, of bronze issued to smiths. A whole world, recorded in clay and lost in a single summer.

options.label: Rebuild the palace and its scribes
The old ways died with the fire

title: The Soldiers Want Their Bronze
text: The levies of {realm} have marched for months and seen neither loot nor pay. Their captains come to {ruler} with hard faces: either the men are paid, or they go home with whatever they can carry.

title: The Priests Grow Bold
text: The high priest has stopped bowing quite so low. The temple's storehouses are fuller than the crown's, its fields wider, and its scribes more numerous. People are beginning to ask who truly rules {realm}.

title: Refugees at the Gates
text: A column of hungry people stands outside {province}: farmers whose wells dried up, townsfolk whose city burned. They ask for land, and bread, and nothing else.

options.label: Put them to work as bondsmen

title: A Fat Harvest
text: The rains came on time for once. The threshing floors of {province} are piled high, and the people sing as they work.

title: Sickness in the Lower Town
text: A fever spreads through the crowded lower town of {province}. The hungry die first, then the old, then the children.

title: A Ship from Afar
text: A round-bellied merchant ship has put in at {province}, laden with oil jars, dyed cloth and a little precious tin. Her captain wants to trade, and would very much like not to be robbed.

title: Donkeys from the East
text: A donkey caravan winds into {province}, the first in many months. Under the felt and the dates, the merchants carry flat ingots of tin.

title: A Rival Claimant
text: A cousin of {ruler}, long thought content, has been feasting the captains and telling anyone who will listen that the throne of {realm} should be his.

title: Horses from the Uplands
text: Horse traders from the high pastures bring tall, deep-chested animals. A chariot behind such a pair would put fear into any line of spearmen.

title: The Oracle Speaks
text: The seer of {province} has fallen into a trance before the whole court and declared that the house of {dynasty} will rule while the sacred spring flows.

options.label: Pay the seer to say it again, louder

title: The Weight of Years
text: {ruler} wakes stiff and slow, and the physicians speak in low voices. There is talk at court of who will stand beside the throne when it changes hands.

options.label: Rest, and let others carry the load
A ruler rules until the end

title: Teaching the Heir
text: {heir} is old enough to learn what a ruler must know. The tutors wait for {ruler} to choose which path the young one will walk.

options.label: Sit at my side in council

title: Bread Riots
text: A mob has broken into the storehouse quarter of {province}. They are not rebels, only hungry, but they are many and they are angry.

options.label: Give out what we have left

title: Bandits on the Roads
text: Deserters and dispossessed farmers have taken to the hills. No caravan crosses {realm} without paying in blood or bronze.

options.label: Pay them to guard the roads

title: Strangers from the North
text: Hill tribes from the north are moving south with their flocks: rough men who speak an odd Greek and fight with long iron swords. They camp at the edge of {province} and wait.

title: The Purple Dye Works
text: The stinking vats of crushed murex shells outside {province} produce the most precious color in the world. The dyers want a bigger yard, the tax collectors a bigger share.

title: Cedar for the God's Barque
text: An envoy from the temple of Amun has arrived, sent to buy cedar for the god's sacred boat. He has more confidence than silver, and speaks of what Pharaoh used to be owed.

options.label: Give the timber as a gift to the god
Mock the envoy and send him home

title: The Tomb Workers Lay Down Their Tools
text: The craftsmen of the royal tombs have not received their grain rations for two months. They have walked off the job and sat down behind the mortuary temple, shouting 'We are hungry!'

title: Robbers in the Valley of Kings
text: A coppersmith has been caught with gold leaf stripped from a royal coffin. Under questioning he names stonecutters, priests, and an official of the city.

title: A Low Nile
text: The nilometer at Elephantine shows the flood barely reaching the old marks. Fields on the edge of the desert will go unwatered this year.

options.label: Offerings at the shrine of Hapi

title: A Good Flood
text: The river rose high and fell gently. The black earth is wet from the desert's edge to the river bank.

options.label: Praise the god and the king

title: Libyans in the Delta
text: Meshwesh herdsmen have crossed into the western delta again, with their cattle and their families and their feathered war chiefs. Some want to fight. More want to stay.

options.label: Drive them back into the desert

title: Aramean Herders
text: Tent-dwelling Aramean clans have driven their flocks into the pastures of {province}. They say the steppe has dried up and they have nowhere else to go.

title: The Lands of Nairi
text: The generals of {realm} remind {ruler} that the kings of old marched every summer into the mountains, returning with tribute of horses, copper and cattle.

title: The Seal of the Great King
text: A refugee scribe from Hattusa brings {ruler} a bronze seal with the winged sun of the Great Kings. Whoever holds it might claim to be their heir.

options.label: Keep it safe in the archives

title: Ox-hide Ingots
text: The furnaces of {province} have cast a new stack of copper ingots, each the shape of a stretched ox-hide. Merchants from three shores are asking for them.

options.label: Keep it for our own smiths

title: A Wise Counselor
text: An old official who served the last great palace has come to {realm} seeking a patron. He knows how a kingdom is counted, fed and taxed.

options.label: Give him a seat on the council
We need no old men's advice

title: A Star with a Tail
text: For nine nights a star with a burning tail hangs over {province}. The priests argue over whether it is a blessing or a warning.

options.label: It is a sign of our greatness
Offer sacrifices to turn aside its anger

title: The Earth Shakes
text: The ground heaved beneath {province} at dawn. Walls cracked, a granary collapsed, and the old palace terrace slid into the ravine.

title: The Great Festival
text: The year turns, and the people of {realm} gather for the great festival of the gods. How lavish will the sacrifice be?

options.label: A hecatomb of a hundred oxen

title: Counting the People
text: {ruler} orders the scribes to count every household, every ox and every jar of oil in {realm}. The people grumble. The tax rolls grow.

title: Merchants Return
text: For the first time in a generation, foreign merchants winter in {province}. The market is loud with strange languages again.

title: The Call of the Sea
text: An old captain offers to take {ruler} on a voyage along the coast: to learn the winds, the harbors, and the islands where pirates hide.

title: The Drums of War
text: Heralds of {other} have declared war on {realm}. The war-horns sound from the citadel, and the levies gather in the square.

options.label: Rally every man who can hold a spear

title: A Stronger Foe
text: {other} fields more spears than {realm} can hope to match. The council is grim. There is bronze in the treasury, and there are men for hire.

title: Spoils of Victory
text: The field is ours. Armor, weapons and pack animals of {other} litter the ground near {province}.

title: Captives
text: Our men have taken many prisoners from the army of {other}, among them sons of noble houses.

title: The Rout
text: Our line broke near {province}. Men threw down their shields and ran. The survivors stream back toward the citadel, and fear goes with them.

title: The Ruler's Wound
text: {ruler} fought in the front rank and took a spear-thrust in the thigh. The wound is ugly. The physicians shake their heads.

title: Smoke Over {province}
text: Raiders from {other} burned the outlying farms of {province}, drove off the herds and carried away whatever they could lift. The survivors want blood.

title: Build Walls
text: The elders of {province} beg {ruler} for walls: real walls of fitted stone, like the citadels of old, so the next raiders find shut gates.

title: They Are Weak
text: The raiders came from {other}, and our spies say {other} is weaker than it looks. The captains say: why only answer raid with raid?

title: The Raiders Return Rich
text: Our warriors are home from {province} with cattle, captives and plunder. They want a feast, and songs about themselves.

options.label: Dedicate the best to the gods

title: Captives from the Raid
text: The raiders bring back a column of captives from {province}: weavers, potters, a smith or two.

title: A Child is Born
text: A child has been born to the house of {dynasty}: {char}. The midwives say the child is healthy and loud.

options.label: A feast for the whole city

title: A Weak Child
text: {char} was born small and quiet, and has not taken well to the breast. The midwives look worried.

options.label: It is in the gods' hands

title: Oaths of Loyalty
text: {ruler} now sits the throne of {realm}. The great men of the realm have come to swear their oaths, and to see what kind of ruler they are swearing to.

title: Whispers Against the New Ruler
text: Not everyone at court is pleased to see {ruler} on the throne. In the barracks and the temple courts, men are saying the old ruler's line is cursed.

title: The Assembly of Warriors
text: The warriors of the tribe gather around the fire to acclaim {ruler}. Custom says a new chief must prove his hand is open and his spear is sharp.

options.label: Give away cattle to every warrior

title: Slaughter the Herds?
text: The granaries of {realm} are empty. The herds remain: the wealth of the realm on four legs. Eat them now, and there will be nothing to breed from next year.

title: Exodus
text: Whole villages around {province} have packed their carts and walked away toward rumors of greener country. Some will become farmers elsewhere. Some will become raiders.

title: Grain from Abroad
text: There is grain for sale in distant ports, for those with silver, dyed cloth or bronze to pay. The merchants know exactly how hungry we are.

title: Warriors Without a Home
text: A chief of the sea folk comes to {ruler} under a branch of olive. His people are tired of the sea. Give them land, he says, and his spears will guard your coast.

title: The Road Ahead
text: The elders of {realm} remember the long road that brought them here. Some say the people should settle and plant. The young warriors say the road is not finished.

options.label: We have arrived. Plant the fields.

title: An Empty Hearth
text: The counselors of {realm} are worried. {ruler} has no spouse, and a ruler without a spouse is a ruler without heirs. Will {ruler} look abroad for a match, or among the great families at home?

options.label: Seek a match abroad (use the Diplomacy panel)
options.tooltip: Open a neighbor's realm and propose a marriage.

options.label: Marry a daughter of a great local family
